council.strength: The project now has one clear idea: entering light through architecture rather than accumulating unrelated interactive effects.
council.concern: Do not allow the late aerial shot or exhibit separation to become louder than the threshold descent.

council.strength: Threshold, radial geometry, bronze, field notation and causal light interaction create an ownable HELIOT language.
council.concern: Protect the field-study framing so the experience does not drift toward generic luxury architecture.

council.strength: The mineral palette, limited type system and restrained calibration accent support the thesis without visual trend-chasing.
council.concern: Keep small notation readable on narrow screens and do not introduce additional decorative systems.

council.strength: The camera has a motivated spatial arc with a real threshold, continuous descent, calm inspection, return and resolution.
council.concern: The signature only works if interface chrome recedes during alignment/descent and the bank stays bounded.

council.strength: The ten chapters move from orientation to awe, explanation, agency, return and ownership without losing navigability.
council.concern: Do not let the anatomy and transmission chapters become information-heavy enough to stall the journey.

council.strength: Aperture changes the world and export; orbit is scoped; sound is explicit; reverse scroll remains meaningful.
council.concern: Keep manual orbit confined to inspection so authored camera continuity remains authoritative.

council.strength: The save-field-study action is a conceptually relevant completion event rather than a generic CTA grafted onto the experience.
council.concern: The artifact must remain easy to discover after a long cinematic journey.

council.strength: The strongest idea is already supported by original local assets, adaptive quality, demand rendering and validated camera clearance.
council.concern: No new high-cost asset production is justified before physical-device WebKit/GPU validation.

council.strength: The same conceptual route, semantic chapter document, touch controls and reduced-motion path are preserved.
council.concern: Continue treating narrow-screen notation density as a review item; never remove meaning to save space.

council.strength: The project uses fictional architecture, original assets and generic field-instrument language without borrowing a specific cultural monument or commissioned building.
council.concern: Maintain the explicit fictional/concept-study framing in documentation and fallback copy.

council.strength: The idea can be explained in one sentence: you physically enter an observatory built from light, manipulate it, and leave with your own field study.
council.concern: When presenting the project commercially, separate observed render costs from claims about physical-device FPS.

council.strength: The experience survives the effect-removal test because threshold, geometry, interaction causality and artifact still carry the idea without particles, autoplay audio or a generic orbit.
council.concern: The easiest way to make HELIOT worse now is to keep adding impressive things. Final cut should prioritize subtraction.

originality.source: Originality comes from reversible physical entry through the architecture, not from surface styling or a novel shader alone.

stress.no3D: PASS WITH DEGRADATION — the semantic/fallback story retains thesis, chapters, light concepts and artifact access, while losing the primary spatial proof.
stress.mobile: PASS — same chapter order and physical route with wider framing.
stress.reducedMotion: PASS — meaning and controls remain available without continuous cinematic interpolation.
stress.halfBudget: PASS — keep threshold/descent, aperture causality and field artifact; cut secondary flourish first.
stress.doubleContent: PASS WITH DEGRADATION — content must be redistributed into quieter study chapters, never the signature descent.
stress.weakAsset: PASS WITH DEGRADATION — original geometry is core; campaign plates are noncritical.
stress.brandSwap: PASS — the threshold/radial/light-instrument language is specifically tied to HELIOT's premise.
stress.signatureRemoval: REQUIRES REVISION — the remaining project is strong but loses its most ownable proof.
stress.skepticalClient: PASS — the value can be defended as spatial proof, not animation quantity.
stress.utility: PASS — index navigation, semantic document and field controls remain accessible.
stress.time: PASS WITH DEGRADATION — even partial visitors encounter place, threshold or light proof depending on entry point.
stress.performance: PASS — adaptive quality and demand frames are native to the implementation; physical-device performance remains a separate verification item.

highestLeverageUpgrades: Physical-device WebKit/GPU validation and tuning if needed.
Final visual capture review after interface-quieting is applied to the signature descent.

warnings: GitHub Actions has previously failed before executing steps, so repository CI should not be represented as green unless steps actually run.
Safari/WebKit and physical-device GPU performance remain unverified in the current environment.
finalCuts: Reduce fixed header/footer/chrome opacity during threshold alignment and descent.
Keep the late aerial reveal calmer than the threshold descent.
Remove any future effect that cannot be justified by light, measurement, architecture or continuity.
Do not add another interactive mode merely to demonstrate Forge capability.
